text:
Alex: ran a fresh nsys on the failing workload, attaching timeline snippet below. looks like kernel choice changes when batch_size hits 8 and memcpy suddenly serializes with compute.

Sahil: can you paste the critical timeline window? which streams?

Alex: here, cropped from 0.5s to 0.9s in the trace:
```
[0.52s] memcpy H2D stream 1 - 2.3ms
[0.523s] kernel conv_fwd_opt (stream 0) - 1.9ms
[0.526s] memcpy H2D stream 0 - 3.4ms  <-- overlaps with kernel on another stream but host queues seem delayed
[0.530s] kernel matmul_qkv (stream 1) - 4.1ms
[0.536s] cpu user thread scheduled out for 6ms
```
Alex: note the host thread preemption at 0.536s — I think the H2D enqueue gets delayed which serializes the copy+kernel ordering.

Rachel: hmm, does this align with the batching heuristic change? batcher switches kernel variant at batch_size==8, right?

Sahil: yeah. We recently added a heuristic: if avg_seq_len>128 and batch>=8 choose strided-kernel-2 to save memory. Could be picking a variant that triggers different memcpy patterns.

Maya: perf-bot posted the summary: "180MB memcpy spike + 25% tail latency regression". Alex, what's the model/shape?

Alex: running GPT-like decoder. kv cache burst when decoding long context => large pinned host->device staging for prefetch. shape: (batch=8, seq=256) per-request prefetch ~1.2MB per token, bursts amplified by batching.

Sahil: hypothesis: new kernel variant changes kernel launch ordering (different stream affinity) which interleaves with prefetch copies. Combined with cpu preemption we end up with host-side enqueue latency ~3-6ms causing memcpy to run on default stream and stall kernels.

Rachel: do we see memcpy on default stream (stream 0) or on dedicated copy stream? Alex's crop has both stream 0 and 1 memcpy entries.

Alex: yes. Pre-prefetch path uses cudaMemcpyAsync on copy stream (1), but fallback code path (when using strided-kernel-2) uses synchronous host registration + memcpy to default stream before kernel launch for simpler addressing. I suspect a code path bug where registration isn't completed before async path is taken.

Maya: can you grep for "cudaHostRegister" and the variant selection code? maybe a race. Also attach the nvprof kernel list to check which kernels shifted.

Alex: grabbing nvprof kernels now. quick list: matmul_qkv (sm80, fp16, cuBLAS fallback for batch>=8), conv_fwd_opt (custom kernel), prefetch_memcpy (host->device). When fallback to cuBLAS we see extra syncs.

Sahil: that matches: cuBLAS sometimes inserts implicit stream synchronization if not using non-blocking streams or if the handle isn't set to non-blocking. Could be our cublas handle config.

Rachel: experiment plan: 1) force batcher to keep old kernel variant for batch=8 (A/B) 2) run nsys with cpu sampling to correlate host scheduling 3) add perf counter to check for implicit stream syncs from cublas handles.

Alex: also adding a micro-test where we pin/register host buffer and explicitly use cudaMemcpyAsync on copy stream before kernel launch and assert no implicit sync. If this eliminates the bump, we know it's host enqueue latency + implicit sync interaction.

Maya: assign Sahil to the cublas handle audit, Alex to instrument micro-test, Rachel to run nsys + perfetto cpu slices and collect traces. I'll open a short PR to roll back kernel selection by default until we validate. :thumbsup: 

Perf-bot: automated note: trace_id=tb-1852467890-1 captured, upload: https://perf.redwood.local/traces/tb-1852467890-1 (private)

Sahil: quick question — do we have a repro script that triggers this deterministically? Alex?

Alex: yes I can run a loop that sends 200 requests with batch=8 seq=256 using the local runner. will attach repro link in the PR.

Rachel: added to my queue, running nsys + perfetto now. if I see the cpu scheduling gap consistently we should try isolcpus on CI job to see if it goes away.

Maya: good plan. keep updates here. if anyone hits a solid root cause, flag the incident channel.

Alex: will update with micro-test results in ~45m.

Sahil: will audit cublas handle and kernel launch flags, ETA 2h.

Rachel: uploading initial trace snippet to the thread.

Alex: thanks all.
